scope: EXACT AND VERIFIED: the 12-bit entity id is assembled as (byte163 bits 5-7) | (byte165 << 3) | (byte166 bit 0 << 11) - the reader SKIPS byte 164 because it uses the byte cursor
why_byte_164_is_skipped: inside 0x66EC30 the multi-byte path sets [+0x20] = remaining_N + [+0x1C] * 8
and [+0x1C] is the BYTE cursor, which the count reader 0x66ED70 had already advanced from 164 to 165
so when the 12-bit read crosses a byte boundary it resumes at byte 165 instead of byte 164
the first 3 bits come from byte 163 (bits 5-7), then 9 bits come from byte 165 and byte 166
so byte 164 is consumed as the COUNT and then skipped by the bit reader
why_this_took_so_long_to_find: the format mixes a byte-addressed field (the count) into the middle of a bit-addressed stream
and the reader's resumption rule uses the byte cursor rather than the bit position, so the two cursors diverge by exactly the byte that was consumed
every attempt to treat the id as a contiguous 12-bit slice at 1309 was therefore off by one byte

the_concrete_recipe.id: write byte 163 bits 5-7 for the low 3 bits of the id, byte 165 for bits 3..10, and bit 0 of byte 166 for bit 11
the_concrete_recipe.example: id = 8 -> byte163 bits5-7 = 0, byte165 = 0x01, byte166 bit0 = 0
